newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan govt reform plan to support Tokyo stocks - EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan govt reform plan to support Tokyo stocks - EPA.

text.p: Tokyo stocks will be bought if the government is able to convince the public that it is serious about carrying out reform, Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso told a news conference on Tuesday.
He said the government's determination was likely to gain public understanding through parliamentary debate on its budget proposals, which was expected to last until around March.
"I think there will be moves to buy (stocks) if the public understands that the government is serious about the various structural reforms," Aso said.
But not all companies would be bought because the various reforms would introduce more competition, he said.
Asked what kind of impacts the falls in Tokyo share prices and the yen's weakness against the dollar would have on Japan's macroeconomy, Aso said there had already been various large impacts.
He said many people said that the falls in share prices had brought about devaluations of companies' shareholdings.

This had also affected banks, which many people fear might be unable to meet capital adequacy requirements, and this was also a factor behind the fall in the value of financial firms' shares, Aso said.
